title: Soft Creamy Polenta with Butter
summary: Coarse polenta cooked low and covered with a pinch of bicarbonate, so it turns silky with only occasional whisking, then finished with butter.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, plus a pat to serve

steps.title: Bring water to the boil
steps.text: Pour the 1100 ml water into the heavy saucepan and bring it to a rolling boil over high heat. Starting with fully boiling water helps the cornmeal swell evenly from the first minute.

steps.title: Whisk in the polenta
steps.text: Rain the polenta into the pan in a thin stream, whisking constantly, then add the salt and the pinch of bicarbonate. Keep stirring until it returns to the boil; the alkali softens the tough outer skin of each grain so it cooks faster and creamier.

steps.title: Cover and steam
steps.text: Turn the heat down to the lowest setting, cover and leave it for 5 min. Then whisk hard, scraping the corners where thick polenta likes to hide, and put the lid back on.

steps.title: Cook low and slow
steps.text: Let it cook another 25 min, whisking every 8-10 min. It is ready when the grains are tender with just a slight bite and the polenta falls from the whisk in a loose ribbon. A splash of hot water brings it back if it stiffens, because cornmeal keeps absorbing liquid as it sits.

steps.title: Finish with butter
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the 30 g butter and the pepper, then taste for salt. Spoon into warm bowls straight away and top each with a pat of butter, since polenta firms quickly as it cools.

tips: Pouring the polenta in all at once is the classic mistake; a thin stream while whisking is what prevents lumps.
Use coarse polenta, not instant; instant cooks in minutes but lacks the sweet corn flavour and texture.
Keep a kettle of hot water nearby to loosen the polenta just before serving.
Leftover polenta sets firm; slice it and fry in a little oil for crisp polenta squares.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container up to 4 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of water or milk, whisking, until piping hot, or slice the firm polenta and fry or grill it. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
